ai.description: Cnemaspis boiei reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include a slender body, granular scales, and a lack of expanded toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis boiei* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of enlarged, spine-like tubercles along the flanks, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Cnemaspis boiei inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks and rocky surfaces at low to mid-altitudes.
ai.behavior: Boie’s Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt small insects on rocky surfaces and tree trunks within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis boiei* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Cnemaspis boiei is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,200 meters.
